questions.q: What did David see from the top of a hill on the second day of his journey?
choices: The village of Essendean far behind him
The city of Edinburgh smoking like a kiln
A great forest stretching to the mountains
The house of Shaws standing in a valley
questions.evidence: the city of Edinburgh smoking like a kiln

questions.q: What did David see on the Glasgow road that filled him with pride?
choices: A great crowd gathered for a country fair
A ship being built beside the road
A regiment marching to the fifes
A fine coach pulled by six horses
questions.evidence: I beheld a regiment marching to the fifes

questions.q: When people in Cramond parish were asked the way to the house of Shaws, how did they react?
choices: They said they had never heard of such a place
They seemed surprised and gave David a strange look
They laughed and pointed him toward the castle
They offered to walk him there for a small fee
questions.evidence: It was a word that seemed to surprise those of whom I sought my way

questions.q: What advice did the man with the cart give David?
choices: To hurry before the gates were shut
To keep clear of the Shaws
To ask the minister for directions
To stay the night at the village inn
questions.evidence: ye'll keep clear of the Shaws

questions.q: The carter asks, "Are ye daft?" What does "daft" mean?
choices: Lost and far from home
Tired from a long journey
Rich and well-dressed
Foolish or out of your mind

questions.q: Why did David ask the barber about Mr. Balfour?
choices: He needed a shave before meeting his uncle
The barber was a cousin of the Balfours
The barber had just come from the house
He knew that barbers were great gossips
questions.evidence: knowing well that barbers were great gossips

questions.q: Why did David keep going toward Shaws even after hearing bad things about it?
choices: He hoped to find a rich treasure hidden in the house
He had come so far that shame and self-respect kept him going
Mr. Campbell had made him promise never to turn back
He had no money left to buy food for the road home
questions.evidence: I was bound, out of mere self-respect, to carry it through

questions.q: What did the house of Shaws look like when David first saw it?
choices: A small farm cottage with a thatched roof
A fine mansion with a garden and gates
A busy castle with soldiers at the door
A kind of ruin with no road and no smoke
questions.evidence: the house itself appeared to be a kind of ruin

questions.q: What did Jennet Clouston do when she showed David the house?
choices: She put a curse on the laird and his house
She told him the laird had died long ago
She offered to carry his letter to the laird
She warned him that the laird kept a fierce dog
questions.evidence: Jennet Clouston has called down the curse on him and his house

questions.q: Jennet's voice rose to "a kind of eldritch sing-song." What does "eldritch" most likely mean?
choices: Cheerful and bright, like a bird
Soft and gentle, like a lullaby
Strange and eerie, like a witch
Low and tired, like an old woman

questions.q: What comforted David after the sun went down as he sat staring at the house?
choices: A thin scroll of smoke rising from a chimney
The sound of a dog barking near the house
A friendly farmer who offered him a meal
A lantern shining brightly by the door
questions.evidence: I saw a scroll of smoke go mounting

questions.q: What was tied across the unfinished main entrance instead of iron gates?
choices: A thorn hedge grown up between the pillars
A row of wooden planks nailed together
A pair of hurdles tied with a straw rope
A heavy chain with a rusty padlock on it
questions.evidence: a pair of hurdles were tied across with a straw rope

questions.q: What flew in and out of the unglazed windows of the house?
choices: Bats
Swallows
Pigeons
Owls
questions.evidence: bats flew in and out like doves out of a dove-cote

questions.q: What did David do after knocking twice and getting no answer?
choices: He climbed in through one of the broken lower windows
He left the letter on the step and walked back to Cramond
He went around the side of the house to look for a back door
He kicked and buffeted the door and shouted for Mr. Balfour
questions.evidence: I began instead to rain kicks and buffets on the door

questions.q: What was the man at the window holding when he first spoke to David?
choices: A walking staff
A lantern
A carving knife
A blunderbuss
questions.evidence: the bell mouth of a blunderbuss

questions.q: What can you tell from the man's question, "Is your father dead?"
choices: He had been told of David's coming by letter
He thought David was a beggar at the door
He was hoping to buy the father's books
He already knew who David's father was

questions.q: What is this chapter mostly about?
choices: David's visit to Edinburgh and the soldiers in the castle
David's growing fear as he hears of Shaws and reaches its gloomy door
David's long walk back to Essendean after being sent away
David's happy welcome at the grand house of his rich relations
questions.evidence: The nearer I got to that, the drearier it appeared
